A.K. Moinul Huq ------ For the Appellant.

Vs.
K.M. Abul  Hossain  ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
2. The case of the plaintiff was that he was appointed as a clerk on 12-11-58 by the defendant and subsequently he was promoted to the rank of Assistant on 24-3-61. That all on a sudden on 4-11-61 he was reverted to his original post and on 8-11-61 he was served with an order of suspension on vague allegation of pilferage, misappropriation and neglect of duties. On 21-12-61 he, was discharged for alleged neglect of duties. The plaintiff appealed to the Chairman of the Corporation but no action was taken and therefore, he served a Pleader's notice upon the Chairman. Thereafter the plaintiff was given personal hearing by the Chairman and the order of discharge was cancelled and the plaintiff was kept on suspension. On, 19-3-62 the plaintiff was served with a notice and asked to show cause in writing as to why he should not be dismissed for loss of some goods and neglect of duties. 

 4. The defendant contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the allegation of the plaintiff. The case of the defendant was that the plaintiff was in-charge of the godown No. 5 of the Corporation. On 12-10.61 it was dictated that goods worth about 20,000/-Take were missing from the go-down and since the plaintiff was in-charge of the godown an explanation was asked for but as he could not give any satisfactory explanation so he was reverted subject to further enquiry and he was suspended. Thereafter on 18-4-62 the enquiry officer heard the plaintiff in person and submitted his report to the Deputy Director holding the plaintiff guilty and perusal of the same the Deputy Director dismissed the plaintiff from service. 

 Mr. A.K. Moinul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant Corporation contended that the appellate Court below misconstrued the evidence of D.Ws.1 and 2 and erroneously come to the conclusion that the Managing Director was the dismissal authority. The learned Advocate pointed out that the law has been now settled that the ordinary law of Master and Servant will apply in the absence of statutory rule and regulation and since it is the common case that no rule has been framed by the Corporation regulating the terms and condition of the service. No exception can be taken in the case of a dismissal of an employee who was found misconduct on proper enquiry. 

 8. Mr. Jamiruddin Sirkar, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff respondent contended that the plaintiff was an employee of the statutory body and in the absence of any rule the proper authority for passing the dismissal order was the Managing Director as contemplated by section 9 of the East Pakistan Small Scale Cottage Industry Act, 1957 (Act 17 of 1957). The learned Advocate further submitted that the Court below did not give any finding as to the misconduct and in that view the dismissal order was illegal. The second point that has been raised by the learned Advocate or the appellant may be disposed of summarily inasmuch as no issue was raised in the trial Court as to the misconduct. The trial Court noted that it was not called upon to give any finding on the point of misconduct and the plaintiff himself has not raised this issue in his pleading. Therefore, this point has no substance. The next question as to the jurisdictional aspect of the case namely whether the Chairman delegated the power of dismissal to the Deputy Director as was claimed by D.W. 2. The trial Court noted that D.W. 2 was not cross-examined at all on this point and the appellate Court conceded that he did not say anything about the power of dismissal and he referred to the delegation regarding the power of appointment and discharge. It is true that D.W. 2 did not refer to the power of dismissal but the purport of his whole evidence was that he found the appellant amongst others responsible for the loss and after giving him an opportunity to explain his conduct he followed the general rule. He explained was the nature of delegation. In view of the fact that no rule was framed by the Corporation and in view of the fact that he followed the rules of the Provincial Government in discharging the plaintiff the trial Court accepted this explanation by recording that all the procedure as laid down in the East Pakistan Government Servant Efficiency and Discipline Rules, 1960 was followed. The learned Munsif has quoted in his judgment "Moreover this has met the ends of natural justice". The purpose of the regulating law is to see the justice is done and no one is condemned unheard. The learned Munsif observed again "Action was taken against the plaintiff after giving him all the opportunity to explain his conduct. The action of the defendant was not arbitrary" As against this the appellate Court below proceeded with a wrong notion following the thread of technical rule that since the plaintiff was appointed by Managing Director his dismissal order must be passed by the Managing Director. There is no legal sanction for following such a line inasmuch as constitutional guarantees were not available to the plaintiff as he does not ensure the description that is mentioned in Article 181 of the 1962 Constitution The ordinary law of Master and Servant is applicable in this case. In the case of Secretary, EPIDC Vs. Md Serajul Haque, reported in 22 DLR (SC) 284 it was observed, 

 "The present case is rather worse than the cited ones inasmuch as the employees in the cited cases being public servants were entitled to the constitutional protection but the respondents here being Servants of the Corporation were not entitled to that protection."
